Shared root

Priyansh Srivastava

Source: vignettes/shared-root.Rmd
shared-root.Rmd

Abstract

In most trajectories the paths share their first cells: a root, and sometimes a segment that several later paths share, a link. This vignette analyses such a trajectory in two ways, with each segment as a path of its own and with the root and the link added to the paths that share them, and shows how the choice of the reference path shapes the results.

Root, link and end paths

multi.lin.sce is a simulated trajectory with three end points, made with dyntoy for the benchmarks of tradeSeq (Saelens et al. 2019; Van den Berge et al. 2020) and analysed with Monocle3 (Cao et al. 2019). Its cells carry a hard path label (group) and the Monocle3 pseudotime (Monocle3_Pseudotime); the Trajectory input vignette shows how to build such labels.

library(scMaSigPro)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(ggplot2)

data("multi.lin.sce", package = "scMaSigPro")
table(colData(multi.lin.sce)$group)
#> 
#>           path_Y_15           path_Y_18 path_Y_18|path_Y_15           path_Y_52 
#>                 307                 676                  43                 498 
#>                root 
#>                 453
tsne <- as.data.frame(reducedDim(multi.lin.sce, "TSNE"))
colnames(tsne) <- c("tSNE1", "tSNE2")
tsne$path <- colData(multi.lin.sce)$group
tsne$pseudotime <- colData(multi.lin.sce)$Monocle3_Pseudotime
p_path <- ggplot(tsne, aes(tSNE1, tSNE2, colour = path)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.5) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
p_time <- ggplot(tsne, aes(tSNE1, tSNE2, colour = pseudotime)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.5) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c() +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
patchwork::wrap_plots(p_path, p_time, ncol = 2)

The cells start in the root, which all three lineages share. One lineage leads straight to the end path path_Y_52; the other two first share a segment, the link path_Y_18|path_Y_15, and then part into the end paths path_Y_15 and path_Y_18. The pseudotime runs from the root through each lineage; every lineage shares it.

The object

The labels are shortened first: the path_ prefix is dropped and the link gets the separator _links_, the default of sc.restruct(). To keep the vignette fast, the analysis uses the first 200 of the 501 genes.

cell_data <- as.data.frame(colData(multi.lin.sce))
cell_data$group <- gsub("path_", "", cell_data$group, fixed = TRUE)
cell_data$group <- gsub("|", "_links_", cell_data$group, fixed = TRUE)
table(cell_data$group)
#> 
#>            root            Y_15            Y_18 Y_18_links_Y_15            Y_52 
#>             453             307             676              43             498

genes <- rownames(multi.lin.sce)[seq_len(200)]
scmp_ob <- create_scmp(
    counts = counts(multi.lin.sce)[genes, ],
    cell_data = cell_data,
    ptime_col = "Monocle3_Pseudotime",
    path_col = "group"
)

Each segment as a path

The first way treats the root, the link and the three end paths as five paths. sc.squeeze() bins each of them along its own pseudotime, so the bins of every segment start at 1:

seg_ob <- sc.squeeze(scmp_ob)
plotBinTile(seg_ob)

The model then compares each segment with a reference segment. With the root as the reference, the terms of every other segment describe how it differs from the root, at the same binned pseudotime. reference names it; without it, sc.set.poly() takes the first path in C-locale (byte) order, here Y_15, whose uppercase Y sorts before the lowercase r of root.

seg_ob <- sc.set.poly(seg_ob, poly_degree = 3, reference = "root")
seg_ob <- sc.p.vector(seg_ob, verbose = FALSE)
seg_ob <- sc.t.fit(seg_ob, verbose = FALSE)
seg_ob <- sc.filter(seg_ob, rsq = 0.6, vars = "groups")
seg_res <- scmpResults(seg_ob)
seg_lists <- as.data.frame(seg_res[, grep("^sig_", colnames(seg_res))])
colSums(seg_lists)
#>            sig_Y_15vsroot            sig_Y_18vsroot sig_Y_18_links_Y_15vsroot 
#>                       120                       120                        97 
#>            sig_Y_52vsroot                  sig_root 
#>                       110                        56

sig_root holds the genes that change along the root, and sig_Y_52vsroot, for example, the genes whose profile in Y_52 differs from that in the root. The overlaps of the lists sort the genes by the segments in which they differ from the root:

plotIntersect(seg_ob)

For example, 17 genes differ from the root in all three end paths but not in the link: along these genes the link carries on the expression of the root, and the end paths leave it. One of them:

plotTrend(seg_ob, link_like_root[1], points = FALSE, lines = TRUE)

This view answers questions about the segments themselves, such as which genes the link turns on, but every segment starts again at binned pseudotime 1, so it does not follow a gene from the root to the end of a lineage.

The root and the link in every path

The second way follows each lineage from the start: the end path Y_15 holds the bins of the root, then those of the link, then its own, and so do Y_18 and Y_52 with the segments on their way. sc.restruct() does this after sc.squeeze(): it copies the bins of the root and of the links into the end paths that share them, shifts the binned pseudotime of the later bins to follow them, and computes the pseudo-bulk counts again.

lin_ob <- sc.restruct(sc.squeeze(scmp_ob),
    end_node_list = list("Y_15", "Y_18", "Y_52"),
    root_node = "root",
    link_node_list = list("Y_18_links_Y_15"),
    verbose = FALSE
)
plotBinTile(lin_ob)

The end paths now share their first bins, and the model compares whole lineages. sc.restruct() puts the paths in the order of end_node_list, so Y_15 is the reference unless reference names another:

lin_ob <- sc.set.poly(lin_ob, poly_degree = 3)
lin_ob <- sc.p.vector(lin_ob, verbose = FALSE)
lin_ob <- sc.t.fit(lin_ob, verbose = FALSE)
lin_ob <- sc.filter(lin_ob, rsq = 0.6, vars = "groups")
lin_res <- scmpResults(lin_ob)
colSums(as.data.frame(lin_res[, grep("^sig_", colnames(lin_res))]))
#> sig_Y_18vsY_15 sig_Y_52vsY_15       sig_Y_15 
#>             54             64             72
lin_ob <- sc.cluster.trend(lin_ob, geneSet = "union", k = 4)
plotTrendCluster(lin_ob, verbose = FALSE)

By hand

sc.restruct() handles a root, links and end paths. For other shapes, build the bins by hand: take the bin table of sc.squeeze() with cDense(), stack the bins of the segments of each lineage with their binned pseudotime shifted, give the stacked bins the label of the lineage in the path column, store the table with cDense<- and compute the pseudo-bulk counts with pb_counts(). For this trajectory, the result is that of sc.restruct():

bins <- cDense(sc.squeeze(scmp_ob))

stack_bins <- function(bins, segments, path) {
    out <- NULL
    shift <- 0
    for (segment in segments) {
        b <- bins[bins$group == segment, , drop = FALSE]
        b$scmp_binned_pseudotime <- b$scmp_binned_pseudotime + shift
        shift <- max(b$scmp_binned_pseudotime)
        out <- rbind(out, b)
    }
    out$group <- path
    rownames(out) <- paste(path, "bin", out$scmp_binned_pseudotime, sep = "_")
    out
}

hand_ob <- sc.squeeze(scmp_ob)
cDense(hand_ob) <- rbind(
    stack_bins(bins, c("root", "Y_18_links_Y_15", "Y_15"), "Y_15"),
    stack_bins(bins, c("root", "Y_18_links_Y_15", "Y_18"), "Y_18"),
    stack_bins(bins, c("root", "Y_52"), "Y_52")
)
#> 'value' has 66 bins instead of 44: the pseudo-bulk counts of the 'Dense' slot are removed; run pb_counts() to compute them for the new bins.
hand_ob <- pb_counts(hand_ob)

restruct_ob <- sc.restruct(sc.squeeze(scmp_ob),
    end_node_list = list("Y_15", "Y_18", "Y_52"),
    root_node = "root",
    link_node_list = list("Y_18_links_Y_15"),
    verbose = FALSE
)
identical(eDense(hand_ob), eDense(restruct_ob))
#> [1] TRUE

Choosing the reference path

The dummies of the model compare every path with the reference path, so the reference decides what the coefficients and the "groups" lists of sc.filter() say: with Y_15 as the reference, sig_Y_52vsY_15 lists the genes whose profile in Y_52 differs from that in Y_15. The full model is the same with any reference, only written in other terms, so the p-values of sc.p.vector() and its non-flat genes do not change, up to rounding. With Y_52, the lineage that leaves the root on its own, as the reference:

ref_ob <- sc.set.poly(lin_ob, poly_degree = 3, reference = "Y_52")
showPoly(ref_ob)
#> [1] "beta0 + beta1*Y_15vsY_52 + beta2*Y_18vsY_52 + beta3*scmp_binned_pseudotime + beta4*scmp_binned_pseudotimexY_15 + beta5*scmp_binned_pseudotimexY_18 + beta6*scmp_binned_pseudotime2 + beta7*scmp_binned_pseudotime2xY_15 + beta8*scmp_binned_pseudotime2xY_18 + beta9*scmp_binned_pseudotime3 + beta10*scmp_binned_pseudotime3xY_15 + beta11*scmp_binned_pseudotime3xY_18"
ref_ob <- sc.p.vector(ref_ob, verbose = FALSE)
all.equal(scmpResults(ref_ob)$p_value, lin_res$p_value)
#> [1] TRUE
identical(scmpResults(ref_ob)$non_flat, lin_res$non_flat)
#> [1] TRUE
ref_ob <- sc.t.fit(ref_ob, verbose = FALSE)
ref_ob <- sc.filter(ref_ob, rsq = 0.6, vars = "groups")
ref_res <- scmpResults(ref_ob)
colSums(as.data.frame(ref_res[, grep("^sig_", colnames(ref_res))]))
#> sig_Y_15vsY_52 sig_Y_18vsY_52       sig_Y_52 
#>             70             66             72

A good reference is the path the others are best described against: the root when the segments are compared, a control or the most common fate when lineages are compared. Without reference, the first path is the first level of the path column when it is a factor, and otherwise the first label in C-locale (byte) order, in every locale; after sc.restruct(), the first path of end_node_list. Naming the reference keeps an analysis the same when the labels change.
